limits: K15.48's (K15.43's): every router call (the load check and the route) under ulimit -v 8000000 (ROUTE_MEMORY_KB) and timeout -k 10 300 (ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S); every route with `--max-passes 2 --timeout 240` after the plugin's flags and before the arm's own. A call that hits ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S or is killed by a signal (exit status 124 or above) is aborted = 1 and not graded. A route the router's own --timeout stopped (result manifest final_state TIMED_OUT) depends on the machine's speed, so its row is not judged in a pair with that arm (validity (b)). Why they stay (`differences`, decided 2026-10-23 at registration): the judged rows are far under the deadline. K15.48's run (target/orchestrator/k1548/out): the longest COMPLETED routes canary-pwr pcb-on 111.2 s, kit-dev-coldfire pcb-on 109.2 s, pcu pcb-on 105.4 s and pcu pcb-off 94.7 s; no call reached ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S (34 x EXIT 0). The switch only ends the fanout earlier (K15.50, target/orchestrator/k1550/runs/q-*: canary-pwr 111.2 s -> 78.4 s with the pair and 82.0 s -> 72.2 s without; kit-dev-coldfire, pcu, wisweep and pcie routed as before). pocketsdr-v3-0 was TIMED_OUT in both arms of K15.30, K15.37, K15.43 and K15.48 (240.1 s and 242.0 s); a longer deadline would change its route and make this measurement differ from K15.48's in more than the switch. It stays in the set, graded for guard (1); validity (b) leaves it out of each pair in which an arm times out, and if the switch lets it complete in both arms of a pair, that pair judges it. If pcu or canary-pwr is TIMED_OUT in any arm the measurement is 'not measured' (must_judge); run the registered run with no other load on the machine. Estimated time: 51 calls (17 rows x 3 arms). K15.48's run: 34 calls in 28 min 20 s (first arm 23:37:52, last log 00:06:12), 1690.5 s of summed phases (pcb-off 789.3 s: route 685.6, KiCad DRC 91.3, prepare 8.8, load 3.7; pcb-on 901.2 s: route 804.4, DRC 84.4, prepare 8.7, load 3.7), so about 10 s of overhead. Scaled to three arms: enhanced about 789 s (K15.48's pcb-off: the switch unset routes as K15.48 did); fix about 700-780 s (K15.48's pcb-off routes less K15.50's cuts on canary-pwr, 82.0 s -> 72.2 s, and loratracker, 50.1 s -> 49.1 s, so about 675 s of routing, and KiCad DRC only on the rows whose session differs from enhanced's, between 2 and 17 rows, about 12-91 s); fix-pair about 870 s (K15.48's pcb-on less canary-pwr 111.2 s -> 78.4 s and loratracker 49.5 s -> 48.7 s: about 771 s of routing and 84 s of DRC). Expected: about 40 min (35-45 min); the bound if every call hit ROUTE_TIMEOUT_S is 51 x about 330 s = 4.7 h

validity: checked before the keep rules, per row and per pair; a row may be left out of one pair's judgement without being left out of the other's. (a) per arm, the arm's settings reached the router: its result manifest (OUT/<row>/<arm>/work/<stem>.result.json) shows in settings_snapshot, for enhanced, no `java_quirks.fanout_two_pass_cycle` (unset, so absent) and neither `pour_fill_target` nor `pour_fill_contacts` true; for fix, `java_quirks.fanout_two_pass_cycle` false and neither pour setting true; for fix-pair, `java_quirks.fanout_two_pass_cycle` false and `pour_fill_target` and `pour_fill_contacts` true (K15.50's arms show these keys: target/orchestrator/k1550/runs/q-canary-pwr-95882f00-pcb-on/work/canary-pwr.result.json). A row whose arm fails (a) is left out of each pair with that arm. A row whose fix session is byte-identical to enhanced's, or whose fix-pair session is byte-identical to fix's (summary grade_shared_with set), is judged as it is (the setting changed no route there) and named; (b) a row is judged in a pair when both of the pair's arms have aborted 0, graded true and final_state COMPLETED; a row COMPLETED in the pair's baseline and TIMED_OUT in its candidate is left out by (b) like any other, its candidate's result depending on the machine's speed, but it is named with both route times and the pair's route-time rule counts it (guard (4) for the pair, clause (vi) for the switch); (c) amendment 1 is written before the first arm and `cargo test -p freerouting-dev --test prereg_k15_51` passes in TREE; (d) a row is judged in a pair when both of the pair's arms route one design: their OUT/<row>/<arm>/summary.json `design_sha256` (the sha256 of the snapshot work/<stem>.kicad_pcb the router reads, plugin-input-ab.sh) are equal, as K15.49 makes them (snapshot.order_zones); a row whose designs differ is left out of that pair's judgement and reported by name with both hashes, and that pair's route-time rule does not count it. A row that fails (a), (b) or (d) for a pair, or whose board is missing, is left out of that pair's judgement and reported by name with its reason (that pair's gate calls get `--left-out ROW=REASON`; guards.py prints each pair's list on its LEFT_OUT_PAIR or LEFT_OUT_SWITCH line); the pair's rule, guards and set noise are then over its judged rows only. The measurement is 'not measured' (decision_table) when, for either pair, fewer than min_boards (3) distinct rows are judged or pcu-76163c7 or canary-pwr-95882f00 is not judged (must_judge), or when (c) fails
guards: (1) in every arm that runs (enhanced, fix and fix-pair) and is graded, judged row or not: manufacturing_breaches = 0, below_minimum = 0 and via_in_pad = 0, absolutely (decided 2026-10-20: routing never breaks the board's manufacturing rules; routing-quality.md, order of importance items 1 and 2); the gate's HARD lines of the verdict pair and the two reported pairs, and summary.json for the rows left out. (2) routing-caused DRC not up: the sum of drc_real over the judged rows in fix-pair is at most fix's. (3) no row worse than its own noise band (K15.14's guard, decided 2026-10-21): on every judged row, fix-pair's kicad_unconnected is at most fix's + the row's band, the totals rule's per-row band (canary-pwr-95882f00 10, every other row max(2, ceil(5 % of its connections)), noise_why). (4) route time: the sum of route_seconds in fix-pair over the judged rows and over every row COMPLETED in fix and TIMED_OUT in fix-pair (validity (b); its fix-pair value is the deadline, about 240.1 s, a lower bound of its time) is at most 1.25 x the sum of fix's over the same rows. Guards (2)-(4) as written judge the pair (fix -> fix-pair); the switch (enhanced -> fix) is judged by keep_rule_by_hand (2), which applies guards (2) and (3) with enhanced for fix and fix for fix-pair, and the route time not up in place of guard (4)
keep_rule: the pair (the verdict pair fix -> fix-pair), read only when the switch is kept: kept when validity holds (at least 3 distinct rows judged, pcu-76163c7 and canary-pwr-95882f00 among them, (c)), guard (1) holds, the signal improves (S: the sum of fix-pair's kicad_unconnected over the judged rows is lower than fix's by more than the set noise sqrt(sum of the bands squared), noise_why; strictly more, as the gate computes it) and guards (2), (3) and (4) hold
keep_rule_by_hand: (1) The records and the gate: from OUT/records.json and OUT/table.md (`python3 -I TREE/tools/bench/k15_all_pours.py collect TREE/docs/roadmap/prereg/K15.51.json OUT`), target/orchestrator/k1551/guards.py's output (OUT/guards.txt: each pair's left-out rows, guard (1) over the three arms, the pair's S and guards (2)-(4), the switch's clauses (i)-(vi), enhanced -> fix-pair for information and the decision table row it reaches) and the gate (TREE's freerouting-dev, heavy_run's last step, with --prereg ROOT's docs/roadmap/prereg/K15.51.json as amended): for the pair `gate ... --baseline OUT/baseline.json --write-baseline`, then `gate ... --baseline OUT/baseline.json`, each with the pair's `--left-out ROW=REASON` (K15.21); for the switch `gate ... --arms enhanced,fix` and `gate ... --arms fix,enhanced` (no --baseline: the baseline records the primary pair), each with the switch's `--left-out`. The verdict pair's 'totals verdict' line is the pair's S, with the set noise it prints; the HARD lines of the three pairs (fix-pair, fix and enhanced as candidates) are guard (1), with summary.json for the rows left out; guards (2)-(4) are summed by hand (guards.py; guard (4) with the rows validity (b) names, compared in tenths of a second, the precision of summary.json route_s). The switch's two calls are read for their 'total' line (S and the set noise), their twice-band line and their HARD lines; their exit status and totals verdict, the registration's `improve` rule, are not read. Validity (a) from the result manifests, (b) from table.md's state column and (d) from each arm's summary.json design_sha256 (records.json does not carry it). (2) The switch's rule (K15.50's measurement; N06's `no-regress` semantics, routing-quality.md 'Correctness fixes', since the switch fixes a flaw in Java's loop and is not expected to cut unconnected), over the rows J that the switch's pair judges, enhanced the baseline and fix the candidate, unc(arm, r) the arm's kicad_unconnected and band(r) as noise_why: (i) S: delta = sum over J of unc(fix, r) - sum over J of unc(enhanced, r); holds when delta <= 0 or delta^2 <= sum over J of band(r)^2 (not worse than the set noise sqrt(sum band^2), equal passing; exact in integers, as the gate's no-regress); (ii) no row worse than twice its band: unc(fix, r) - unc(enhanced, r) <= 2 x band(r) for every r in J; (iii) guard (1) in every graded arm of every row (all three arms); (iv) guard (2): the sum over J of fix's drc_real is at most enhanced's; (v) guard (3): unc(fix, r) <= unc(enhanced, r) + band(r) for every r in J; (vi) the route time is not up: the sum of fix's route_seconds over J and over every row COMPLETED in enhanced and TIMED_OUT in fix (counted as guard (4) counts the candidate's timeouts; its value is the deadline, a lower bound) is at most the sum of enhanced's over the same rows (ratio at most 1.000; compared in tenths of a second). The switch is kept when the measurement is measured and (i)-(vi) all hold; (vi) is the switch's purpose (K15.50: the cycle cost about 24 s on canary-pwr). (3) For information only, guards.py also prints enhanced -> fix-pair over the rows both pairs judge (unconnected, drc_real, route time); it is not judged

decision_table.not measured: for either pair (the verdict pair fix -> fix-pair or the switch's enhanced -> fix), fewer than min_boards (3) distinct rows judged or pcu-76163c7 or canary-pwr-95882f00 not judged, or validity (c) fails (a row left out of a pair by validity (a), (b) or (d) does not by itself make the measurement 'not measured': it is reported by name and the pair's other rows are judged): K15.51 and K15.50 stay [~] naming the rows and reasons; nothing changes in the product (the switch stays in neither profile, both pour settings opt-in); the rows are run again only after the cause is fixed (a longer timeout_s or a fix), under an amendment naming it, with nothing else changed
decision_table.breach: the measurement is not 'not measured' and guard (1) fails in any graded arm of any row (judged or not, in any of the three arms): K15.51 and K15.50 stay [~] naming the arm, row and items; the breach is fixed in an item of its own, then the registered run repeats at the fixed commit under an amendment; until then the switch stays in neither profile and `router.pour_fill_contacts` and `router.pour_fill_target` stay opt-in, unset in both profiles. Whose defect it is: a breach in enhanced is a defect of today's default (the plugin's default options, both pour settings and the switch unset) and leaves both plugin options as they are; a breach in fix that enhanced lacks on the row is a defect of the switch (`router.java_quirks.fanout_two_pass_cycle=false`), fixed before the switch is measured again, and leaves both plugin options as they are; a breach in fix-pair that fix lacks on the row is a defect of the pair, and the plugin does not offer `router.pour_fill_contacts` until the fix (K15.37's option: the options.py field and its to_args line, the Advanced tab's checkbox, its plugin tests and the plugin handover's row are removed; K15.30's `pour_fill_target` option, measured alone, stays). A breach that the arm before it on the row has too (fix after enhanced, fix-pair after fix) is that earlier arm's defect (decided 2026-10-20: fix gains, don't remove them; never ship below-minimum copper)
